title: Utility Types
summary: TypeScript ships a set of built-in generic types that transform existing types without rewriting them. The most useful in React are: Partial<T> (all fields optional — perfect for update payloads and form state), Pick<T, K> (keep only listed fields — great for component props that show a subset of a model), Omit<T, K> (drop listed fields — useful when creating records before an ID is assigned), and Record<K, V> (typed object map — replaces any for dictionaries and caches). These utility types compose well: Partial<Pick<Movie, 'rating' | 'genre'>> gives a partial update type for just two fields.
keyPoints: Partial<Movie> — every field becomes optional: useful for PATCH payloads and form drafts
Required<Movie> — every field becomes required: opposite of Partial
Omit<Movie, 'id'> — drop the id field (e.g. before creation, when the DB assigns it)
Record<string, Movie> — an object whose keys are strings and values are Movies
Utility types compose: Partial<Omit<Movie, 'id'>> for an optional create payload
All utility types produce new types — they do not mutate the original interface

options: { id?: number; title?: string; rating?: number }
{ id: number; title?: string; rating?: number }
{ id?: number } | { title?: string } | { rating?: number }
exercises.answer: { id?: number; title?: string; rating?: number }
exercises.explanation: Partial<T> makes every property optional by adding ?. All three fields become optional, so an empty object {} is valid as Partial<Movie>. This is ideal for update/PATCH functions where you only send the fields that changed.

exercises.prompt: You want a type that has only the title and poster fields of Movie. Which utility type gives you this?
exercises.explanation: Pick<T, K> creates a new type that keeps only the listed keys from T. Pick<Movie, 'title' | 'poster'> gives { title: string; poster: string }. Omit does the opposite — it removes listed keys.

exercises.prompt: When creating a new movie, the database assigns the id. Which type represents a movie without an id?
exercises.explanation: Omit<T, K> removes the listed keys from T. Omit<Movie, 'id'> gives { title: string; rating: number; poster: string } — exactly the shape needed to create a movie before the server assigns an id.

exercises.prompt: You want a typed in-memory cache where keys are movie IDs (numbers) and values are Movie objects. Which type is correct?
exercises.explanation: Record<K, V> creates an object type with keys of type K and values of type V. Record<number, Movie> means numeric keys and Movie values. It is more readable than the index signature syntax and more idiomatic for plain objects.

exercises.prompt: A function receives only the fields the caller wants to update. Which type should its parameter be?
exercises.explanation: Partial<Movie> makes all fields optional, so the caller can pass just { rating: 9.0 } or { title: 'Dune: Part Two', rating: 8.5 }. The function must still receive the id to know which record to update — that is typically a separate parameter.

exercises.prompt:
What does this composed type represent?
type MovieDraft = Partial<Omit<Movie, 'id'>>
options: A Movie with all fields required except id
A Movie with no fields at all
A Movie where all fields except id are optional
An object that can only have an id field
exercises.answer: A Movie where all fields except id are optional
exercises.explanation: Omit<Movie, 'id'> removes id. Partial<...> then makes the remaining fields optional. The result is a type where title, rating, poster etc. can all be omitted — useful for a form state where the user fills in fields one at a time.

exercises.prompt: Using utility types, define: (1) NewMovie — Movie without id, (2) MovieUpdate — all Movie fields except id are optional, (3) MovieCache — a Record keyed by number:
exercises.code:
interface Movie { id: number; title: string; rating: number; poster: string }

// Define NewMovie, MovieUpdate, MovieCache here
exercises.answer:
interface Movie { id: number; title: string; rating: number; poster: string }

type NewMovie = Omit<Movie, 'id'>
type MovieUpdate = Partial<Omit<Movie, 'id'>>
type MovieCache = Record<number, Movie>
exercises.explanation: NewMovie uses Omit to remove id. MovieUpdate composes Partial and Omit — first remove id so it cannot be accidentally changed, then make the remaining fields optional. MovieCache uses Record for a numeric-keyed object of Movies.
